abstract: The interplay between RNA viral dynamics and innate immunity remains poorly understood, mainly because RNA viruses trigger highly nonlinear cytokine responses. We address this using infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a major poultry pathogen, as a model system. We developed a set of mathematical models and compared those with experimental data from two IBV strains infecting chicken macrophages.By model fitting and supervised Machine Learning we reveal that positive feedback in interferon- production is essential to reproduce the dynamics of one IBV strain but likely absent in the other. We further provide strain-specific estimations of key parameters such as infection rates, production and decay rates of virus and cytokine levels. Notably, different strains produced distinctive cytokine profiles, highlighting feedback as a key determinant of strain-specific immune signatures. Our results establish a quantitative framework for dissecting host-virus interactions and uncover cytokine feedback as a generic yet underappreciated feature in models of RNA virus kinetics.
